arxiv-2107-06456.title: AID-Purifier: A Light Auxiliary Network for Boosting Adversarial Defense
arxiv-2107-06456.creator: Duhun Hwang, Eunjung Lee, Wonjong Rhee
arxiv-2107-06456.description: Abstract We propose an AID-purifier that can boost the robustness of adversarially-trained networks by purifying their inputs. AID-purifier is an auxiliary network that works as an add-on to an already trained main classifier. To keep it computationally light, it is trained as a discriminator with a binary cross-entropy loss.

arxiv-2108-03346.title: The area operator and fixed area states in conformal field theories
arxiv-2108-03346.creator: Wu-zhong Guo
arxiv-2108-03346.description: Abstract The fixed area states are constructed by gravitational path integrals in previous studies. In this paper we show the dual of the fixed area states in conformal field theories (CFTs). These CFT states are constructed by using spectrum decomposition of reduced density matrix ρ A \rho_{A} for a subsystem A A .

arxiv-2204-00335.title: Fact-nets: towards a mathematical framework for relational quantum mechanics
arxiv-2204-00335.creator: Pierre Martin-Dussaud, Titouan Carette, Jan Głowacki, Vaclav Zatloukal, Federico Zalamea
arxiv-2204-00335.description: Abstract The relational interpretation of quantum mechanics (RQM) has received a growing interest since its first formulation in 1996. Usually presented as an interpretational layer over the usual quantum mechanics formalism, it appears as a philosophical perspective without proper mathematical counterparts.

arxiv-2306-14687.title: GSMorph: Gradient Surgery for cine-MRI Cardiac Deformable Registration
arxiv-2306-14687.creator: Haoran Dou, Ning Bi, Luyi Han, Yuhao Huang, Ritse Mann, Xin Yang, Dong Ni, Nishant Ravikumar, Alejandro F. Frangi, Yunzhi Huang (🖂)
arxiv-2306-14687.description: Abstract Deep learning-based deformable registration methods have been widely investigated in diverse medical applications. Learning-based deformable registration relies on weighted objective functions trading off registration accuracy and smoothness of the deformation field. Therefore, they inevitably require tuning the hyperparameter for optimal registration performance. Tuning the hyperparameters is highly computationally expensive and introduces undesired dependencies on domain knowledge.

arxiv-2410-24093.title: Superconducting order parameter structure in the nematic phase of iron-based materials
arxiv-2410-24093.creator: M. M. Korshunov +, Yu. N. Togushova ∗
arxiv-2410-24093.description: Abstract We consider the effect of the nematic order on the formation of the superconducting state in iron pnictides and chalcogenides. Nematic order with the B 2 ​ g B_{2g} symmetry is modelled as the d d -type Pomeranchuk instability and treated within the mean-field approach.

arxiv-2602-06025.title: Learning Query-Aware Budget-Tier Routing for Runtime Agent Memory
arxiv-2602-06025.creator: Haozhen Zhang, Haodong Yue, Tao Feng, Quanyu Long, Jianzhu Bao, Bowen Jin, Weizhi Zhang, Xiao Li, Jiaxuan You, Chengwei Qin, Wenya Wang
arxiv-2602-06025.description: Abstract Memory is increasingly central to Large Language Model (LLM) agents operating beyond a single context window, yet most existing systems rely on offline, query-agnostic memory construction that can be inefficient and may discard query-critical information. Although runtime memory utilization is a natural alternative, prior work often incurs substantial overhead and offers limited explicit control over the performance-cost trade-off.

pmc-10541896.creator: Luka Traven, Sandra Marinac-Pupavac, Paula Žurga, Željko Linšak, Sandra Pavičić Žeželj, Marin Glad, Darija Vukić Lušić
pmc-10541896.description: The following study aims at assessing the health risks associated with the consumption of the most commonly consumed seafood in the north-western part of Croatia due to the presence of heavy metals. Samples of seafood were collected and analysed for lead (Pb), cadmium (Cd), and mercury (Hg) content.

pmc-11519566.title: Study on the strength influence mechanism and cracking mechanism of stone powder-cement floor grouting materials
pmc-11519566.creator: Xinming Chen, Diantao Zheng, Huazhe Jiao, Liuhua Yang, Yangyang Rong, Jinyu Sun
pmc-11519566.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Underground grouting is a concealed project, and it is difficult to test the strength of grouting stones in engineering practice. Aiming at the problems of high confined water pressure and strong water-richness of the roadway floor, a pressure filtration test device was developed, and a PFC2D uniaxial compression model was established to study the variation law of stone strength and crack evolution mechanism of grouting materials under different grouting pressures.

pmc-11547129.title: Changes in Gut Microbial Composition and DNA Methylation in Obese Patients with NAFLD After Bariatric Surgery
pmc-11547129.creator: Antonella Agodi, Claudia Ojeda-Granados, Andrea Maugeri, Martina Barchitta, Ornella Coco, Salvatore Pezzino, Gaetano Magro, Gaetano La Greca, Francesco Saverio Latteri, Sergio Castorina, Stefano Puleo
pmc-11547129.description: This study investigates the effects of bariatric surgery on non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) by examining the interplay between gut microbiota, epigenetics, and metabolic health. A cohort of 22 patients undergoing sleeve gastrectomy (SG) was analyzed for changes in gut microbial composition and DNA methylation profiles before and six months after surgery.

pmc-13367408.title: Enhancing Transparency, Auditability, and Reproducibility of Deduplication in Systematic Reviews: Tutorial for the Rayyan Method and Systematic Auto Resolver
pmc-13367408.creator: Mimi M Kim, Amin M Shanaa, Hossam Hammady, Mohammad Aboelnour, Robert Ayan, Matthew Balcarras
pmc-13367408.description: Deduplication across search results is one of the earliest and most critical steps in the systematic review methodological process; yet, existing solutions often lack the transparency, auditability, and reproducibility required by rigorous systematic review standards. Many automated deduplication tools introduce bias through opaque, nonconfigurable algorithmic decisions, while also potentially removing relevant references through false positive identification.
